highlights.title: Mathematicians Hate AI. They Can’t Quit It
highlights.summary: Powerful AI models have created an existential risk to the field, but researchers can’t stop relying on them because they’re too useful.
body: Mathematician Tristan Buckmaster believes OpenAI used his work to rush ahead and beat him to solving a legendary math problem with a $1 million bounty.
But that’s not been enough for him to stop using the company’s models—and he’s not the only mathematician that feels that way.

“Even if you don't agree with any of this, you're kind of stuck. With AI being so useful, it's hard to completely prevent oneself from using it,” Buckmaster tells WIRED. “These companies have a monopoly, and there is not much choice,” he adds.

In the week and half since the New York University professor accused OpenAI of copying his approach, Buckmaster has been using the company’s coding agent Codex to tidy up his research papers. When he has time to do math (which he says is rare, since the fallout thrust him into the spotlight), the tool has been helping him understand the logical steps OpenAI’s agents might have taken to get from his earlier workings to the final proof.

body: The Godolphin colt had been second to the Michael Dods-trained Arapaho Gold in the Listed Rose Bowl Stakes over course and distance in July, after which Arapaho Gold came out to land the Gimcrack.

body: Deadline revealed the existence of the Lollipop Chainsaw movie on Sept. 18, hot off the announcement of Lollipop Chainsaw 2 Back2Back at Tokyo Game Show earlier in the week. Its report describes the movie as a prequel to the first game and an "R-rated action comedy" about the series' protagonist, Juliet Starling.

It's still early days for the project, so it currently just has a creative and production team consisting of a grab bag of international filmmakers and producers. Dragami Games told Deadline that it's "pleased to be working with such an experienced and passionate international team — one that understands what makes Lollipop Chainsaw special while embracing the opportunity to create something new." No director or major Western film studio appears to be attached to the Lollipop Chainsaw movie at this time.

highlights.title: ‘American Hostage’ Review: Jon Hamm and Giovanni Ribisi in an MGM+ Kidnapping Thriller With Lots of Potential but Little Payoff
highlights.summary: Shawn Ryan and Eileen Myers ('The Night Agent') adapt the podcast focusing on a 1977 kidnapping in Indianapolis and the trusted radio host caught in the middle.
body: MGM+ ‘s American Hostage is a TV show based on a podcast about the power of radio, a chaotic media-hopping smorgasbord that feels oddly appropriate when you watch the eight-part series that flirts with a number of contemporary topics but ends up being mostly well-acted, over-extended nostalgia for landline telephones and manageable institutional corruption.

The series is set in 1977, and if you’ve seen Gus Van Sant’s 2025 Dead Man’s Wire, you already know a somewhat fictionalized version of the story, which was the subject of the first season of the American Hostage podcast from Criminal Content.

Hamm plays Fred Heckman, an Indianapolis news radio legend. Heckman, who has a wonderfully supportive marriage to Barbara ( Mireille Enos ) plus three kids who are irrelevant to the series, is described on bus ads as “the most trusted voice in news.”

Heckman has largely given up on the reporting that launched his career and, after 22 years in Indianapolis, he’s weighing a lucrative offer to move to CBS Radio in New York City. Then he becomes part of the biggest story to hit Indianapolis in years.

highlights.title: US fashion CEO resigns after physically restraining animal rights activists
highlights.summary: Steven Kolb of the Council of Fashion Designers of America was filmed during an altercation at New York fashion week. The chief executive of the Council of Fashion Designers of America, Steven Kolb, has resigned after he was filmed physically restraining two animal rights activists during an…
body: “After 20 years leading the CFDA, I have made the difficult decision to step down as CEO and president,” Kolb said in a statement. “I am enormously proud of what we have built together and believe this is the right moment for both me and the organisation to begin a new chapter.”
Kolb had been placed on leave on Tuesday pending a review of an incident during a COS show at New York fashion week on Sunday.

In a video, Kolb could be seen trying to restrain two People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (Peta) protesters who attempted to disrupt the show in a demonstration against the use of wool by the H&M group, which owns COS.

Kolb pushed a protester, identified as Mason Melito, and covered his mouth. Kolb also wrestled a second protester to the ground, using his arms and a leg to restrain her and putting his hand over her mouth.

highlights.title: Does AI need an antitrust exemption so it doesn’t kill everyone????
highlights.summary: Today on Decoder, we’ve got the first of a two-part series on the future of business, and I’m talking with Jonathan Kanter, the former antitrust chief for the US Department of Justice in the Biden administration.
body: The biggest story in tech right now is the spiraling debate about AI safety and regulation. Researchers at the big AI labs including Anthropic and Google DeepMind have quit in noisy ways, saying the models pose real threats and safety isn’t being taken seriously across the industry. Other researchers have said the chance of AI killing us all is greater than 10 percent, and the CEOs of all these companies have issued various calls to slow down development and develop regulation, including asking for antitrust exemptions so they can all coordinate on safety issues.

That is a lot of ideas, and I am especially curious about the antitrust piece, which has led to accusations that these companies are seeking regulatory capture, attempting to form a cartel, and even somehow finding a way out from investor pressure ahead of their IPOs.

Jonathan brought huge antitrust cases against Google, Apple, and Ticketmaster during his time as antitrust chief, and along with Lina Khan, led what amounted to a full reboot of American antitrust policy. As you’ll hear him say, he won those cases against Google and Ticketmaster, and that case against Apple is still live in the Trump DOJ, surprising many.

highlights.title: Cardiff beat Charlton to record first win of the season
highlights.summary: Cardiff's long wait for a first win on their Championship return is finally over after Republic of Ireland star Jack Moylan scored a brace in their 3-1 home victory over Charlton.
body: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Cardiff City and Charlton Athletic at the Cardiff City Stadium on Saturday; Jack Moylan double steers Bluebirds to a first victory of the campaign.

The Bluebirds had gone a record-equalling seven games without a win despite dominating a number of their previous matches, but they were full value for their triumph after taking a 2-0 lead in the opening quarter against a Charlton side that came into the fixture sitting in sixth place with only one league defeat.

Moylan scored the first goal in the eighth minute, teed up Yousef Salech for the second in the 24th and then thundered in his second, and Cardiff's third, in the 61st after Tyreece Campbell had reduced the deficit.

Charlton's physicality and pressing meant it took Cardiff some time to settle into their passing rhythm and the first chance of the game fell to Miles Leaburn after good work down the left flank from Karlan Grant and Campbell.

highlights.title: Paramount's New High Fantasy Epic is Already the Streaming Sleeper Hit of 2026
highlights.summary: Sega has been making video games since 1973 and owns the rights to everything from modern hit franchises like Yakuza and Persona to arcade mainstays like Crazy Taxi and Streets of Rage. The possibilities were endless. McMahan didn't hesitate. He chose Golden Axe.
body: Mike McMahan was working as a script doctor on the Sonic the Hedgehog movies when he received an incredible offer: A Sega executive approached him and asked if there were any other properties the storied game studio owned that he'd want to adapt into a series.
"I'm very old," McMahan tells Polygon by way of explaining his somewhat surprising choice. "When the NES came out, that was amazing for me, and before then, I played an insane amount of Golden Axe."

For the unfamiliar, Golden Axe is a series of beat-'em-up fantasy video games released by Sega. The first one debuted in 1989 as an arcade cabinet. Seven sequels and spinoffs followed, with the last being 1995's Golden Axe: The Duel, though a new game was announced by Sega at the 2023 Game Awards and is seemingly still in development.

In other words, Golden Axe is not exactly a hot commodity, but that didn't stop McMahan, whose memory of the game dates back to his time at a Chicago summer camp where Golden Axe and a few other arcade cabinets were rigged up so you could play them for free.

highlights.title: ‘Anchors Aweigh’ Review: A Cynical Comedian Reflects on His Youth in an Abridged Mockumentary
highlights.summary: In Matt Barats’ “Anchors Aweigh,” a caustic alt-comedian is left adrift after his failed proposal, prompting him to revisit old footage from his college days and ruminate on his arrested development.
body: Matt Barats brings mordant wit to both sides of the camera, for better or worse.

When the acerbic lead rents a boat on a Marina by a New York airport, the movie gestures toward a mockumentary in the vein of John Wilson, or a send-up of Ross McElwee, but its secondary and tertiary characters — marina residents whom Barats interacts with — seldom stick around long enough to make a lasting impact. It isn’t long before the story snaps back towards malformed romance, the self-conscious tone of which does little more than exacerbate its narrative flaws.

highlights.title: The Black women who choose to have children on their own: ‘We’re going in eyes open’
highlights.summary: With growing support networks online and in person, these moms say they’re changing the narrative around Black single motherhood. When Chamise Alston was ready to have a child, she connected her computer to her TV and scrolled through profiles with her best friend, dismissing people who seemed like…
body: That winter day in 2023, Alston and her friend chose a donor who would help her become pregnant with her now 16-month-old daughter. As a Black woman, she felt empowered taking control of her reproductive destiny.
“I always wanted to be a mom,” said 40-year-old Alston. “Once I realized that there was a route for me to be a mom, sans a relationship, that’s always been my mission.”

Alston is part of a growing number of Black women opting to be single moms by choice (SMBC) through IVF, intrauterine insemination and adoption. Studies show that SMBCs are most likely to be financially stable, educated women in their late 30s. While Black women who choose solo parenting fit a similar profile as their white peers, they face unique challenges. Along with navigating stigmas around Black single motherhood, they also contend with a limited number of Black and brown sperm donors, and sometimes face discriminatory experiences from hospital staff during labor and delivery.

highlights.title: Google's Gemini AI hacked three companies in security test
highlights.summary: The AI model accessed the internet and guessed credentials to three websites, a Google official told the BBC.
body: Google's AI model Gemini autonomously hacked into three companies during a test of its cyber-security capabilities, the company has said, in what is thought to be the first known case of it carrying out such an act.
Gemini found "public information online and guessed credentials to access websites it thought were part of the test", a Google official told the BBC, noting that in each instance "the model stopped".
The affected companies were informed about the breaches, which happened in May.

It comes after renewed public scrutiny over the pace of AI development, as some tech firms calling for a slowdown over concerns over its potential threat to humanity - but not all companies or experts agree.

highlights.title: Vals, backed by Andreessen Horowitz, is looking to become the gold standard for AI benchmarking
highlights.summary: Vals AI is hoping to make AI benchmarking a more neutral and trustworthy resource in a world increasingly inundated by AI models.
body: Benchmarking has become the industry norm for how AI companies validate their models’ capabilities and, when the metrics swing in their favor, stand out from competitors and advertise their superiority. In other words, good benchmarks pretty much always mean good PR.
Unfortunately, companies have also figured out how to outwit legacy benchmarking systems — many of which are older, and not built to measure the capabilities of modern models.

Vals, a startup formed in 2024, says that it is on a mission to fix this very imperfect system. In the span of less than two years, the company has established itself as a notable presence in the tech industry and, last year it managed to secure a seed round led by 8VC and Bloomberg Beta. Then, last month, after a period of rapid growth, it raised $40 million in a series A led by Andreessen Horowitz.

highlights.title: West Ham fight back from two down to draw fiery derby at Millwall
highlights.summary: West Ham battled back from 2-0 down to draw 2-2 at arch-rivals Millwall in a fiery renewal of one of football's most famous derbies, which included a late red card for Mohamadou Kante.
body: The half-time sub had helped change the game for the visitors, arrowing into the bottom corner from 25 yards to launch the comeback. The Hammers then levelled on 80 minutes when Konstantinos Mavropanos headed in at the back post and looked set to push on for a winner.

But Kante brought down Kyrell Lisbie with a last-man foul after he had been caught in possession to receive the fourth red card in the past seven meetings between these sides and Lyndon Dykes blasted over a last-gasp chance for the Millwall to clinch it.
It was a dramatic conclusion to a game which lived up to its billing, 14 years on from the last Dockers derby.
The home side overwhelmed West Ham in the first half. Close-range goals from Caleb Taylor and Camiel Neghli from Dykes long throws summed up their physical approach.

highlights.title: The Blood of Dawnwalker Modders Aren’t Missing the Point – They Just Love the Game
highlights.summary: Modders are extending The Blood of Dawnwalker's 30-day time limit to allow more time to complete every questline. But while this goes against the developer's vision, it shouldn't be seen as vandalism.
body: This is an IGN opinion piece from Mat Jones, who thinks everyone’s made too big a deal out of experience-altering mods, and wouldn’t replay a video game ever, even if he were forced to do so by vampires holding his family hostage.

I’ve spent the weeks since The Blood of Dawnwalker’s release nodding at headlines about how the time-pressured quest to rescue lead character Coen’s family – which is on a controversial 30-day timer – is the heart of the design, and that anyone looking to extend that clock with a mod wouldn’t be having the intended experience.

But, after reading that the developers themselves aren’t so bothered about the timer that they’d definitely want to add it in again – that a Dawnwalker sequel could strip out this mechanic and still inexorably be a Dawnwalker game – I’ve interrogated my own assumptions. I wonder if we’ve been giving anyone who’d roll back a couple of 0s on the odometer too hard a ride. Is the example of the “irresponsible modder”, someone incapable of understanding that developer intent should supersede any possible alteration, a fantasy?

But while this goes against the developer's vision, it shouldn't be seen as vandalism.

highlights.title: ‘Trees Are Watching’ Review: Eva Green Fights A.I. Generated Horrors in Self-Serious Misfire Boarded by Martin Scorsese
highlights.summary: Bahman Ghobadi directs some fascinating performances in “Trees Are Watching,” his horror movie based on the Kurdish legend of people being reborn as trees and living second lives as furniture.
body: Iranian new wave mainstay Bahman Ghobadi tries his hand (and his prompts) at a midnight movie.

The film begins with a flashback to three young Kurdish girls in Mardin, Turkey discussing the aforementioned superstition, before one of them, Darya (Green), returns years later from abroad with her Deaf, nonverbal daughter Connie (Neva Kuş) to perform anthropological research in the area. Kuş is a firecracker of a performer, adding lively dimensions to the chilling atmosphere when things go bump in the night, and Connie begins hearing strange, unsettling sounds through her hearing aid.

A pair of tall trees sway outside the home Darya has rented, a modern expansion of where her childhood friends Nihal and Spin used to live. Inside, Darya’s dog acts aggressively toward an ornately carved chair, which Connie soon claims has been moving on its own. Before long, the chair becomes a specter of sorts, seemingly possessed by a spirit from Darya’s past, which unravels in vivid flashbacks that don’t entirely seem motivated — they’re Nihal and Spin’s memories for the most part, not Darya’s — but which detail an intriguing backstory nonetheless.

highlights.title: Don’t be afraid to be masculine, laugh more, and phone your mum: letters to our sons, by Stephen Graham, Riz Ahmed, Danny Dyer and other wise men
highlights.summary: The Adolescence actor and the psychologist Orly Klein asked fathers to write to their sons. The results – from famous dads to the wisdom of strangers – were moving and motivating. Here’s a selection. What can I say?
body: What can I say? From the moment you and your sister were born my heart has been full of a love I never thought was humanly possible. As a baby you were filled with wonder and so much energy. You had a beautiful, mischievous and inquisitive nature, which has always made me smile. You were climbing, running and jumping everywhere. You’d walk into a room wearing shoes that were four times, five times, 10 times too big for you … Sometimes they were ye mother’s.

The sound of your laughter is one of the most beautiful compositions made by nature. I am so blessed to be a part of your life, and our friendship is something I hold dear to my heart. That beautiful bouncing boy has grown into a man who brightens up a room whenever he walks into it.

I have had the pleasure of watching you grow, of watching you learn the lessons of life, like how you conducted yourself when your heart was broken for the first time. To watch you navigate that pain with compassion and come out the other side appreciating your worth without holding on to any resentments, showing your vulnerability to me and your mother and allowing us to guide you through – that was truly admirable.
points: The Adolescence actor and the psychologist Orly Klein asked fathers to write to their sons.
The results – from famous dads to the wisdom of strangers – were moving and motivating.
From the moment you and your sister were born my heart has been full of a love I never thought was humanly possible.
As a baby you were filled with wonder and so much energy.

If you buy something from a Verge link, Vox Media may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

Some of the claims in the video may be based on speculation and assumptions, but many of the core concerns are real and pervasive. While LG was the focus of the video, every TV company is tracking what you do, collecting that data, and sharing it with its partners. And we agree to it — even if we don’t realize it.

TV prices have come down significantly over the years, to the point where some companies are selling them at a loss. But they make up that shortfall selling user behavior data they collect from the OS. It’s why Walmart bought Vizio in 2024.

highlights.summary: Recently unsealed court documents in the New York Times ' case against OpenAI and Microsoft are pretty damning. The companies' own documentation warned that it was starting a "doom loop" that would damage the web, characterized its scraping of data to train its models as the "largest theft of labor…
body: The companies knew they were driving us toward Google Zero, and did it anyway.

Many of the most eye-catching quotes from the document come from Microsoft’s Director of Applied Science, Brent Hecht. Though, the company has tried to distance itself from Hecht’s assertions. Microsoft spokesperson Alex Haurek told The Verge that “These comments reflect one employee’s individual perspective, are not a legal analysis, and do not represent the company’s views.”

In a separate court filing, Jordan Usdan, GM for Data Strategy and Ops at Microsoft AI, characterized Hecht’s role as adversarial. He said that Hecht “holds divergent, academic, and forward-looking views about how data ecosystems for AI should operate and is employed at Microsoft to bring asymmetrical, futuristic, and academic points of view … nor is he someone who speaks for Microsoft specifically as to his theoretical views on AI’s potential effect on content creators.”
But whether or not Microsoft wants to own these comments, it’s clear that this came true. Google Zero is real! AI is eating the web!

body: It’s AI CEO against AI CEO, and things are changing by the day.

Anthropic and OpenAI had already been dropping hints that they and other labs were working on some kind of industry framework. Appearing pro-regulation looked like both a good PR move and, potentially, a way for companies to address fallout from progressively more concerning hacking incidents.

For now, any government involvement in this process looks like a non-starter. The Trump administration has attacked the idea of a safety crisis in AI, calling it a “hoax.” The AI world itself is also divided. Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg quickly came out against limiting companies’ autonomy, and earlier this week, the Wall Street Journal reported that Zuckerberg, Musk, and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang scuttled proposals for an industry-funded independent regulator for the AI industry — akin to the ​Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA), a private nonprofit regulator in finance. But parts of the industry aren’t giving up on the idea, including OpenAI.

highlights.title: Here’s How an AI Slowdown Could Actually Be Enforced
highlights.summary: Even if big AI companies agree to a pause, ensuring that nobody tries to sneak ahead could prove tricky.
body: Many AI researchers seem to firmly believe that the technology they are developing could someday prove very dangerous. What’s less clear—even among AI’s technical elite —is precisely how to keep these mercurial algorithms in check.

In recent years researchers have thrown around all sorts of ideas for preventing AI from turning nasty. They include less controversial plans such as tighter government regulations, new ways of measuring progress, and probing the inner workings of models, as well as more outlandish proposals like placing tracking devices inside GPUs, and even ceremonially destroying large numbers of AI chips.
With political and public pressure now growing for a more measured approach to building AI, however, the answer to keeping AI safe is still unclear.

“We need to start treating this as a research problem,” says Raymond Douglas, an AI researcher at the University of Toronto and coauthor of a new report titled Pacing the Frontier, A Research Agenda, which warns that slowing down AI development remains an unsolved puzzle. “We don't really understand what our options even are or what they will do.”

highlights.title: Forget Your 100-Hour RPGs, Action Games Are Having a Moment
highlights.summary: Gaming is a trend-based medium. Often, when a hit game turns into a generational success story, you can see it shape the industry in real-time as studios try to copy its notes. In recent history, we’ve seen that with an influx of two types of games: open-world games and Soulslikes.
body: While both of those are still very much in fashion, 2026 has seen an unexpected trend shift: Straightforward action games are having a moment. Some of the year’s best, or at least most high-profile, games are trading in vastness and RPG customization for something more focused. Call it a throwback to an older era of gaming, but it’s a welcome shift for anyone who has been put off by how demanding big-budget games have become over the years.

That charge is being led, in no small part, by Capcom. The publisher has had a statement year by releasing hit after hit that buck conventional wisdom. Rather than going big for Resident Evil Requiem, for instance, Capcom delivered a lean 11-hour game. Half of that is a straight-up action shooter, as Leon S. Kennedy blasts his way through a compact slice of Raccoon City. Not a second of gameplay goes wasted, nor is any single idea repeated more times than it needs to be.

highlights.title: When Hollywood’s Major Studios Threatened to Leave California — For Florida
highlights.summary: A Democratic Socialist was running for California governor and the studio chiefs balked and said they'd pack up their moving trucks and leave. They were bluffing in 1934. Now...
body: Southern California seems to have been terraformed by the Creator to attract the motion picture industry: the mild, sunny weather conducive to outdoor shooting; the boundless variety of natural scenery (ocean, mountains, desert, farmlands) that can double for any location on earth; the diverse population of ready-made extras, and, at least in the first decades, the open shop policies of the city fathers (no pesky trade unions).

Little wonder that the pioneers of the medium ditched the cold, clammy, and crowded precincts of New York and New Jersey to light out for the picture-perfect vista. Soon enough, modern factories staffed by a pool of extraordinarily talented artists sprang up to manufacture quality-controlled product. Why would any filmmaker want to leave such prime real estate and glamorous expertise?

highlights.title: Learning another language may be one of the best ways to keep your brain healthy
highlights.summary: Learning another language is a highly complex mental activity. It requires people to remember words, distinguish unfamiliar sounds, recognize patterns, work out grammatical rules, and retrieve the right expression at the right moment.
body: Could all this mental activity also help keep an aging brain healthier? Research suggests it can.

Concerns about memory and dementia can send aging adults looking for ways to exercise their brain and maintain cognitive function, whether it is solving crossword puzzles or playing a musical instrument. Language learning might not seem like the same kind of brain exercise, but it is a complex activity that engages several mental processes at once.
I am a linguist who studies language acquisition, use, and loss. My new book, Beyond Words: How We Learn, Use, and Lose Language, examines language and the mind across people’s lifespans.

Research increasingly suggests that language learning and bilingualism can offer cognitive benefits —including for older adults. Learning another language can also create opportunities for communication and social connection.

highlights.title: India forces caller-ID apps to feed spam reports to telcos
highlights.summary: Truecaller says the one-way sharing requirement would hand a commercially valuable proprietary asset to telecom operators.
body: India has extended its anti-spam regime to require caller-ID and call-management apps to share users’ spam reports with telecom operators, prompting spam-blocking app maker Truecaller to call the ruling anti-competitive.

On Friday, the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI), the country’s telecom regulator, amended rules governing commercial communications, making it mandatory for caller-ID and call-management apps that let users flag calls as spam or junk to send those reports to a blockchain-based platform maintained by telecom operators. The platform tracks commercial communications and enforces anti-spam rules.

The change, TRAI said, is intended to broaden the pool of spam reports available for action against spammers, effectively connecting reports collected by apps with the telecom industry’s enforcement infrastructure.

However, Truecaller told TechCrunch that it sees this requirement as a “one-way exchange” that is “anti-competitive,” arguing that it transfers commercially valuable data from call-management apps like itself to telecom operators.

body: I'll admit to being a little worried at the beginning of my preview after learning it would consist of two boss battles fought in groups of four. After all, the majority of my co-op experience comes from RuneScape, a 25-year-old MMORPG primarily played with a mouse, and nobody wants to let their team down.

But first came the character selection. There were four options available in my demo: two focused around melee combat, two ranged. Both combat styles offered one character with healing-focused abilities which I immediately discounted - too much responsibility. The archer with a mechanical arm though? Inflicting heavy damage from a distance while taking care of any nasty surprises was definitely something I could do. Decision made, it was time to discover how my chosen role would actually play out in battle.
